metadata.note: The Lake Shore and Michigan Southern Railway (formed 1869: the Lake Shore Railway absorbed the Cleveland and Toledo 11 Feb 1869, merged with the Michigan Southern and Northern Indiana 6 Apr 1869, absorbed the Buffalo and Erie 22 Jun 1869) ran Buffalo - Cleveland - Toledo - Chicago and a web of Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan and Indiana branches until it merged with the New York Central and Hudson River on 22 Dec 1914 to form the New York Central Railroad. Vanderbilt control from 1869 (stock majority 1877) did not change who ran the trains: the LS&MS operated everything west of Buffalo until 1914. This layer draws only LS&MS-operated years (1869-1914 or shorter); post-1914 service belongs to New York Central features, and the pre-1869 constituents (Buffalo and Erie, Cleveland and Toledo, Erie and Kalamazoo, Michigan Southern / MS&NI) are not drawn here.
metadata.colour: #8E4A7A, new for this company (no feature anywhere in data/ used it, checked programmatically 2026-10-30); distinct from New York Central grey #5C677D.
metadata.ownership_split: Every feature ends at or before the 22 Dec 1914 merger into the New York Central; the main line's continuation is new_york_central.geojson nyc-water-level-albany-chicago, which was split the same day so that it no longer draws Buffalo - Chicago as NYC before 1914 (see that file's metadata.lsms_split_2026_10_30). Leases that started LS&MS operation and set a feature's start: Mahoning Coal 1873, Detroit Hillsdale and South Western 1 Jul 1881, Fort Wayne and Jackson Nov 1882, Chicago and Canada Southern 8 Nov 1879, Union Stock Yards branch 1891 (from the IC). NOT splits: 1877 Vanderbilt stock majority; the CP&A's 1868 rename to Lake Shore Railway; the J&F's 1909 fold into the JF&C (still LS&MS-operated).
metadata.omitted: Per the research report: [10] Sharon Branch (one weak 1902 Guide anchor; omitted as the report recommends); [13] Franklin - Brookville (no LS&MS-era passenger year); [14] unused; [24] Goshen Branch Goshen - Sturgis - Findley - OMITTED: the only 1890-1914 support is the Feb 1890 lease date (a lease is not a passenger train) and a 6 Jun 1915 NYC timetable note on a michiganrailroads page whose text is muddled with the Fort Wayne branch; there is no positive LS&MS-era passenger year, so under the 'omit rather than invent' principle it waits for the 1915 timetable itself; [25] Fayette Branch east, Slocum Jct - Dundee - Grosvenor (single 1879 anchor; omitted as recommended); [27] Dundee Branch (no LS&MS-era passenger evidence); [28] Chicago suburban service Chicago - Whiting (same track as the main line; 1893 anchor only); [30] Elkhart and Western (unresolved, NONE); [31]-[37] pre-1869 constituents (out of scope for this layer); [38]-[44] not LS&MS-operated or freight (Dunkirk Allegheny Valley and Pittsburgh, Lake Erie Alliance and Wheeling, III/CI&S, Cincinnati Northern and CW&M, Battle Creek - Findley, Cleveland Short Line, P&LE).
metadata.freight_only_check: 2026-10-30: no freight-only feature or segment. The 1903 Carson - Brookfield low-grade line (freight) is not drawn - the Ashtabula - Andover and Youngstown features follow the original high-grade passenger line. The Mahoning Coal RR is drawn only for the Fowler-confirmed passenger years 1875-1893. Abandonment years (Goshen 1960/1980, Morenci - Fayette 1941, Ypsilanti last freight 1962) are not used as passenger ends.
metadata.horsecar_check: 2026-10-30: no LS&MS-era animal traction known; the Erie and Kalamazoo's 1836-37 horse era predates this layer.
metadata.conflicts: Kalamazoo, Allegan and Grand Rapids lease to the LS&MS: 1868 (Grand Rapids Public Library) vs 1869 (Kalamazoo Public Library) - not resolved; the feature starts at the 1 Mar 1869 opening to Grand Rapids either way. Andover - Jamestown connection 1871 vs Ashtabula - Andover 1872 (sources differ on which piece opened when). Jamestown and Franklin lessee before 1869: CP&A (Wikipedia body) vs 'LS&MS' (anachronistic; Wikipedia intro). Detroit - Toledo: traced 57.2 mi vs Fowler 64.3 mi.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends - last CONFIRMED year, not a known end, each almost certainly ran to the Dec 1914 merger but withheld until a 1905-1914 timetable is cited (a 1910-1914 Official Guide would close most): Youngstown Branch (lsms-youngstown-branch) 1893; Andover - Jamestown and Jamestown - Franklin (lsms-andover-jamestown, lsms-jamestown-franklin) 1890; Franklin - Oil City (lsms-franklin-oil-city) 1890; Detroit - Toledo (lsms-detroit-toledo) 1907 - Detroit - Chicago through trains after the c.1908/1913 terminal moves still unconfirmed; Monroe Branch (lsms-monroe-branch) 1913; Jackson Branch (lsms-jackson-branch) 1910; Fort Wayne Branch via Hillsdale (lsms-fort-wayne-branch-via-hillsdale) 1899; Fort Wayne Jct - Bankers original routing (lsms-fort-wayne-branch-via-bankers) 1890, with undated mixed trains after; White Pigeon - Kalamazoo and Kalamazoo - Grand Rapids (lsms-white-pigeon-kalamazoo, lsms-kalamazoo-grand-rapids) 1893; Fayette Branch (lsms-fayette-branch) 1910. Other open questions: when the Northern Division west of Sandusky was abandoned and whether 1869-1871 through trains ran via Norwalk (Sandusky - Toledo drawn from 1872 on a citation-needed Wikipedia claim); the Kalamazoo and White Pigeon's opening year (White Pigeon - Kalamazoo withheld 1869-1874); whether Mahoning Coal passenger trains began with the Aug 1873 opening; Jonesville - Albion 1872 start; the exact c.1890 date of the Fort Wayne branch reroute via Hillsdale; Chicago stock-yards branch dates (Fowler's prose note only); Goshen Branch 1915 timetable (see omitted); every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this layer is an estimate.
metadata.geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror (railway degree-tiles plus ways tagged old_railway_operator~NYC|New York Central|Lake Shore|LS&MS|Penn Central|Conrail|Canada Southern), OSM rail-trails and OpenHistoricalMap railway ways for lifted stretches, routed with opstrace.py, simplified with douglas_peucker(8 m) and trim_reversals. Probed spellings 2026-10-30: no OSM way carries old_railway_operator LS&MS / Lake Shore / Lake Shore & Michigan Southern; 3,309 ways in the region carry NYC, 7 'New York Central', 5 'NYC then CR', 1 'Conrail'. Hand-pinned waypoints: Cleveland Union Depot, Toledo Union Depot, Brush Street (Detroit), Hillsdale, Allegan, North Lansing, Englewood, Jackson MI, Ray IN, Grosvenor MI, and the Mahoning Coal grade points at Williamsfield/Kinsman/Fowler/Brookfield (Nominatim returned counties for Huron, Sandusky, Elkhart, Porter, Jefferson, Fowler, Franklin, Monroe, Clinton, Jackson, Hillsdale, Schoolcraft, Otsego, Allegan, Fayette - each re-queried with a county qualifier or pinned).

segments.note: Report blocks [1]-[3]: Buffalo (Exchange Street) - Dunkirk - Erie - Ashtabula - Painesville - Cleveland (Union Depot) - Berea - Elyria - Vermilion - Huron - Sandusky, the eastern half of the Lake Shore route. The LS&MS was formed in 1869 (Lake Shore Ry absorbed the Cleveland and Toledo 11 Feb 1869, merged with the MS&NI 6 Apr 1869, absorbed the Buffalo and Erie 22 Jun 1869 - Wikipedia LS&MS), and ran every train on this line until the 22 Dec 1914 merger into the New York Central. Vanderbilt control from 1869 (stock majority 1877) was common control, not common operation: the NYC&HR ran the through trains only east of Buffalo. Cleveland - Sandusky had been open since 24 Oct 1853 (Wikipedia Cleveland and Toledo). Fowler: NY line 137 west of Buffalo z 1890t / a 1910t, stations y (1875); OH line 1 stations y, several a (1907t); Amherst, Brownhelm, Vermilion, Bay Bridge a (1907t). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (Rule 3) (corridor aggregate; no LS&MS timetable count was made).

START 1875: the Aug 1873 opening is not shown to have included passenger trains. END 1893 [OPEN]: Passenger service confirmed to 1893 by the 1893 Official Guide (Fowler's z tag). This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source seen dates when LS&MS passenger service actually stopped, and the line very probably carried passengers to the Dec 1914 merger. Do not extend without evidence. (abandonedrails' 'last passenger train 1962' for the Youngstown Branch is unverified.) headway_min is an ESTIMATE (Rule 3).

properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE - not taken from any LS&MS timetable running time; a typical 1870s-1910s figure for this class of line. Rule 3.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap rail, routed with opstrace.py, 2026-10-30
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 0.6 mi on untagged OSM rail along 40th Street west from the LS&MS/Rock Island main line; it stops about 0.5 km short of the Union Stock Yards point (Halsted Street area, hand-pinned) because no grade is mapped further - the last ~0.3 mi into the yards is NOT drawn. No straight-line legs. Documented mileage unclear (see the Drexel Boulevard feature).

segments.note: Report block [29], west part: 39th Street - Union Stock Yards. Fowler IN 20B note: operated by the LS&MS '39th St>Stockyards until 1908' after the IC's 1882-1891 operation (not drawn); z stations = the 1893 LS&MS suburban timetable; 'replaced by El line'. Dates rest on that note; only 1893 is a timetable snapshot. headway_min 60 is an ESTIMATE (Rule 3).
